hypothesis_text: Targeted prompt revisions improve the worker pool: we identified the three worst-performing workers from a 50-trial sweep, rewrote their system prompts, and the same three workers improved by 18% on the next sweep. Prompt iteration on poor performers is effective.
flaw_description: Workers selected because they had the lowest scores in one noisy sweep are exactly the workers most likely to score higher next sweep regardless of any intervention — pure regression to the mean. A proper test re-runs all workers with no intervention as a control; the prompt-revision effect is whatever improvement exceeds that baseline.
expected_critique_targets: selected on the dependent variable (low scores)
regression to the mean explains expected improvement
need a no-intervention control on the same workers
context: n=50 trials with noisy per-trial scoring; three worst selected for intervention.
